body.statement:
For every \(I\in\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\), let \(\mathcal D\subseteq C\) be the set of the \(\ell\ge1\) original response blocks occurring in \(g\), and for \(c\in\mathcal D\) put \(N_c=|R_c|\), \(r_c=\operatorname{rank}(A_c)\), and \(L_c=\sum_{j=0}^{r_c}\binom{N_c}{j}\). If every nontrivial variable in \(V\) is binary, then the exact sharp endpoints \(\underline\theta,\overline\theta\) and rational attaining finite SCMs are computable without a width assumption. For any omitted block \(c_*\in\mathcal D\), one complete algorithm enumerates the vertex lists only for \(c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}\) and, for each resulting tuple, solves one bounded rational linear program over \(K_{c_*}\) for either endpoint. Its bit complexity is
\[
\left(
 \sum_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}L_c
 +\prod_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}
       |\operatorname{ext}(K_c)|
\right)\operatorname{poly}(B),
\]
and the product in this display is exactly the number of outer linear programs for either endpoint. Dovetailing the choices of \(c_*\) attains the minimum of the displayed instance bounds up to a polynomial factor. In particular, choosing \(c_*\) with largest \(L_c\) gives
\[
B^{O((\ell-1)(1+\log B)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B),
\]
so \(\ell=1\) is an exact polynomial-time case. Every query-irrelevant block is completed by rational linear-program feasibility rather than support enumeration.
body.justification: This gives a second exact regime when a useful decomposition is unavailable but the query touches few original roots.
body.gap: Arroyo et al. obtain polynomial-cardinality column generation for one intervention; the proposed logarithmic-square rank bound covers several explicitly represented relevant blocks and an objective of degree at least three.
body.consumer: A canonical optimizer can dispatch sparse-block binary queries even when its measured scalar response width is large.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(I\in\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\).  By \(\text{def:no-width-input-class}\), the graph is finite and acyclic, every exogenous root has at most two observed children, all response coordinates and all raw equality rows are explicitly present, the observational table is compatible, and the query is block-affine.  Delete singleton-valued observed arguments from the response tables; this changes neither a response-table set nor an equality row.

We first bound the exact raw rank of an original block.  Suppose that \(c\) has two nontrivial children.  For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), let \(d_j\) be the number of nontrivial binary observed arguments of the \(j\)-th child's response function and set \(h_j=2^{d_j}\).  There are \(2^{h_j}\) deterministic binary response functions for that child, so completeness of the response list gives
\[
N_c:=|R_c|=2^{h_1+h_2}. \tag{1}
\]
There are at most \(2^{d_1+d_2}=h_1h_2\) joint external-parent contexts.  Sharing an observed parent, or having an observed edge between the two children, can only reduce this number because an internal child value is then not a freely chosen external context coordinate.  At a fixed context a deterministic response tuple produces exactly one of at most four joint binary child outputs.  Hence the corresponding raw equality rows partition \(R_c\) into at most four supports, and the total number of raw rows is at most \(4h_1h_2\).  Rank is at most the number of rows, and therefore
\[
r_c:=\operatorname{rank}(A_c)
 \le 4h_1h_2
 \le (h_1+h_2)^2
 = (\log_2N_c)^2, \tag{2}
\]
where the middle inequality is equivalent to \((h_1-h_2)^2\ge0\).

If \(c\) has one nontrivial child with \(d\) nontrivial binary observed arguments, put \(h=2^d\).  Then \(N_c=2^h\), there are at most \(h\) external contexts, and each has two output rows.  Thus
\[
r_c\le2h=2\log_2N_c. \tag{3}
\]
A block with no nontrivial child has constant dimension and rank.  Combining the cases yields the uniform bound
\[
r_c\le4(1+\log_2N_c)^2. \tag{4}
\]

For later use define
\[
L_c:=\sum_{j=0}^{r_c}\binom{N_c}{j}. \tag{5}
\]
The \(K_c\) clause of \(\text{lem:rational-factor-vertices}\) says that a point of \(K_c\) is a vertex exactly when the columns of \(A_c\) indexed by its positive support are linearly independent.  Consequently its positive support has size at most \(r_c\).  Testing every support of size at most \(r_c\), solving the associated rational system exactly, retaining precisely the nonnegative feasible solutions, and removing exact duplicates therefore produces the complete list \(\operatorname{ext}(K_c)\).  Exact Gaussian elimination and rational comparison take polynomial bit time per tested support because the full system is part of \(I\).  The same lemma gives \(O(B^2)\)-bit numerators and denominators for every retained coordinate.  Thus this list is generated in \(L_c\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations.  Moreover,
\[
L_c
 \le (N_c+1)^{r_c+1}
 \le B^{O((1+\log B)^2)}, \tag{6}
\]
because \(\text{ass:complete-response-list}\) charges at least one input bit to each of the \(N_c\) response records, whence \(N_c\le B\), and (4) applies.

Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq C\) be the set of blocks occurring in at least one monomial scope of \(g\); by definition \(|\mathcal D|=\ell\).  Fix for the moment one block \(c_*\in\mathcal D\).  Generate the complete vertex list just described for every \(c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}\), and do not generate a support list for \(c_*\).  For a tuple
\[
v_{- *}\in
 \prod_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}
       \operatorname{ext}(K_c), \tag{7}
\]
block-affinity from \(\text{ass:block-affine-query}\) gives an explicitly computable rational affine function
\[
x\longmapsto g(v_{-*},x)=\alpha_{v_{-*}}+p_{v_{-*}}^{\mathsf T}x,
\qquad x\in K_{c_*}. \tag{8}
\]
There are at most \(B\) serialized monomials and at most \(B\) factors in each, and all substituted vertex coordinates have \(O(B^2)\)-bit encodings.  Hence the coefficients in (8) have encoding length polynomial in \(B\).

By \(\text{lem:rational-h-representations}\), \(K_{c_*}\) is a nonempty bounded rational polyhedron with an explicit encoding of length at most \(B\).  Apply \(\text{lem:exact-rational-linear-programming}\) to minimize or maximize (8) exactly.  If a basic optimizer is desired, first compute the optimal value, intersect \(K_{c_*}\) with the resulting rational optimal-face equality, and then lexicographically maximize the \(N_{c_*}\) coordinates by at most \(N_{c_*}\le B\) further exact linear programs.  The final point is unique: two distinct survivors would differ first in some coordinate, contradicting maximization at that lexicographic stage.  A unique point of a face is a vertex of that face and hence a vertex of \(K_{c_*}\).  The \(K_c\) clause of \(\text{lem:rational-factor-vertices}\) then shows that this basic optimizer is rational with \(O(B^2)\)-bit coordinates.  Thus each inner optimization in (8) costs \(\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations.

It remains to prove that these finitely many linear programs return the global endpoints, rather than merely candidates.  By \(\text{lem:rational-h-representations}\), every \(K_c\) is compact, so the finite product is compact; the polynomial \(g\) is continuous, so its minimum and maximum are attained.  Starting from a maximizer, hold every other block fixed and apply the preceding exact linear optimization argument to one block in \(\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}\).  Replacing that block by a vertex optimizer cannot decrease the value.  Repeating over all such blocks leaves a global maximizer whose listed blocks lie in (7).  The final maximization over \(K_{c_*}\) is exactly (8).  The same argument with minimization cannot increase the value.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{z\in\prod_{c\in C}K_c}g(z)
 &=\max_{v_{-*}\text{ satisfying }(7)}
     \max_{x\in K_{c_*}}g(v_{-*},x),\\
\min_{z\in\prod_{c\in C}K_c}g(z)
 &=\min_{v_{-*}\text{ satisfying }(7)}
     \min_{x\in K_{c_*}}g(v_{-*},x).
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Blocks outside \(\mathcal D\) do not occur in \(g\).  For each such block, apply \(\text{lem:exact-rational-linear-programming}\) to the zero objective over its nonempty rational polyhedron and use the same lexicographic refinement to obtain one rational basic feasible point.  There are at most \(B\) blocks, so all these feasibility completions together cost \(\operatorname{poly}(B)\); no support of an irrelevant block is enumerated.

For a fixed \(c_*\), support generation costs
\(\sum_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}L_c\operatorname{poly}(B)\), while (9) invokes, for either endpoint, exactly
\[
E_{c_*}:=
\prod_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}
 |\operatorname{ext}(K_c)| \tag{10}
\]
outer rational linear programs.  Exact evaluation, comparison, and backpointer storage for each tuple have polynomial bit cost because all intermediate rational encodings are polynomial in \(B\).  The total fixed-branch bound is therefore
\[
\left(
 \sum_{c\in\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}}L_c+E_{c_*}
\right)\operatorname{poly}(B). \tag{11}
\]
Running the \(\ell\) choices of omitted block in round-robin and stopping when the first correct branch completes multiplies the least bound in (11) by at most \(\ell\le B\); this proves the stated minimum instance bound up to its polynomial factor.  Alternatively, for the uniform advertised rate choose \(c_*\) with largest \(L_c\).  Since every \(L_c\ge1\) and \(|\operatorname{ext}(K_c)|\le L_c\), equations (6), (10), and (11) give
\[
\left(
 \sum_{c\ne c_*}L_c+E_{c_*}
\right)\operatorname{poly}(B)
 \le
B^{O((\ell-1)(1+\log B)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B). \tag{12}
\]
When \(\ell=1\), both the sum and the product over \(\mathcal D\setminus\{c_*\}\) are respectively zero and one.  Thus no relevant-block support is enumerated, (8) is a single rational linear program for each endpoint, and the complete procedure is polynomial-time.

Finally, combine an optimizing relevant tuple from (9) with the rational feasible points selected for the irrelevant blocks.  This produces rational points of \(\prod_{c\in C}K_c\) attaining both extrema.  By \(\text{prop:canonical-semantics}\), those extrema equal \(\underline\theta\) and \(\overline\theta\), and each concatenated feasible point induces a normalized finite independent-root SCM compatible with \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and having the same interventional query value.  Hence both sharp endpoints are exact, rationally attained, and computed without a width assumption or an implicit response-column oracle.
